title: Sodium intake and all-cause mortality over 20 years in the Trials of Hypertension Prevention
authors: Cook NR, Appel LJ, Whelton PK
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
population: TOHP I and II participants aged 30 to 54 years with prehypertension not assigned to an active sodium intervention, with sodium intake averaged from 24-hour urine collections during the trials (three to seven scheduled, one to seven collected; mean 4.4 in TOHP I and 3.5 in TOHP II)
funder: TOHP I and II were supported by NHLBI cooperative agreements HL37849, HL37852, HL37853, HL37854, HL37872, HL37884, HL37899, HL37904, HL37906, HL37907 and HL37924. The TOHP Follow-up Study was supported by NHLBI grant HL57915 and American Heart Association award 14GRNT18440013. The NHLBI and AHA had no role in design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, manuscript preparation or the decision to submit.
result: 272 deaths. Hazard ratio per 1000 mg/24 h of sodium 1.12 (95% CI 1.00 to 1.26), with no evidence of a J-shaped or nonlinear relation. Versus 3600 to <4800 mg/24 h: <2300 mg/24 h 0.75 (0.45 to 1.26; 23 deaths among 312 participants), 2300 to <3600 mg/24 h 0.95 (0.70 to 1.29), 4800 mg/24 h or more 1.07 (0.75 to 1.54). In the randomised comparison, 251 deaths; hazard ratio 0.85 (0.66 to 1.09) for sodium intervention.
